items.title: Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Rescue teams have recovered 1010 bodies and brought out more than 11800 people so far. Around 4000 remain unaccounted for, including about 590 foreigners from 39 countries.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Fifth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods
items.summary: Rescue teams from India, China, and Korea are working with Nepali forces to clear tunnels blocked by mud and boulders. Forensic teams from those countries plus Singapore have arrived to help with DNA identification, while most pilgrims from the Mount Kailash route have already returned.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fifth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods

items.title: Foreign nationals — missing, rescued, or contacted (NDRRMA, 1 Sep)
items.summary: Families looking for news on foreign nationals after the Bhote Koshi flood in Rasuwa can check the Department of Tourism tourist list. A final situation update is dated 30 August at 19:00.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — X post (1 September 2026)

items.title: Embassy of India — identification of mortal remains (1 Sep 2026)
items.summary: Families can check photos and descriptions of remains from the Nepal floods on the police disaster portal. Relatives should email DNA details or call the Nepal police and embassy helplines for matching and handover steps.
items.citation: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — Press Release (1 September 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Rescuers have brought out over 10,000 people so far, including more than 300 foreigners. About 4,200 people remain unaccounted for, with 903 bodies recovered.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Nepal Police — DNA profiling for unidentified remains
items.summary: Relatives of people missing in the Rasuwa and Bhote Koshi floods can give DNA samples to help identify recovered bodies. First-degree family members in Nepal can provide a blood sample and photos at the Nepal Police Hospital or a district police office.
items.citation: Nepal Police HQ — Information on DNA Profiling for unidentified Dead Bodies (31 Aug)

items.source: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA)
items.title: NDRRMA — Bhotekoshi water level rising again (31 Aug)
items.summary: The Bhotekoshi River water is rising again. People in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and nearby areas should stay careful.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — public warning via official channels

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)
items.summary: After the Bhote Koshi floods, 734 bodies have been recovered and about 2,498 people remain unaccounted for. Rescue teams have brought out more than 8,000 people so far, with search and relief work still underway in the affected districts.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River on August 26, and teams have recovered 626 bodies while about 2400 people are still missing. Over 4450 people have been rescued so far, including 187 foreigners, with search efforts continuing in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal’s Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August and caused major damage and loss of life. Rescue teams have recovered 538 bodies so far, with hundreds of locals and tourists still missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: Rescue teams and helicopters are searching the mudslide area at Gyirong Port after three people were killed and 558 remain missing. More crews arrived Thursday with supplies to help clear the blockage and reach those still unaccounted for.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal’s Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August, destroying homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure and leaving many people missing. So far 359 bodies have been recovered and 596 people from 33 countries remain unaccounted for.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026

items.title: NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood
items.summary: Nepal's foreign ministry has opened an emergency room to help with foreign nationals missing or affected by the Rasuwa floods. Call or message +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 between 7am and 10pm.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood

items.title: Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation
items.summary: India’s foreign ministry has opened a 24-hour control room in Delhi for the Nepal floods. Families can use the listed phone and WhatsApp numbers to reach them or the Indian embassy in Kathmandu.
items.citation: MEA press release — Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods struck Nepal this morning, killing people and damaging homes, roads and other infrastructure. So far 72 bodies have been recovered and 403 people are reported missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
